prompts.subject: science
prompts.prompt_text: Generate a video visualizing electron orbital arrangement inside an atom. Show the nucleus at the center with protons and neutrons, then depict s, p, and d orbitals as probability clouds at different energy levels. Electrons should appear as moving points within their respective orbital shapes, with each shell clearly labeled (1s, 2s, 2p, etc.).

ground_truth.correct_answer: Accurate depiction of atomic electron orbitals with correct shapes and energy level ordering
key_visual_elements: central nucleus with protons and neutrons
p-orbitals as dumbbell shapes along x/y/z axes
key_steps: Label each orbital and energy level

prompts.rubric_criteria: 9-10: Orbital shapes are scientifically accurate (s=sphere, p=dumbbell, d=clover), energy levels correctly ordered, electron probability density clearly visualized. 7-8: Orbital shapes are mostly accurate with minor errors, energy levels are mostly correct, and electron probability density is generally well-represented. 5-6: Some orbital shapes are correct, but there are noticeable inaccuracies in others; energy levels may be mislabeled or unclear, and electron density visualization is inconsistent. 3-4: Atom-related imagery present but orbital shapes are incorrect or electrons shown as simple circular orbits (Bohr model) instead of quantum mechanical clouds. 1-2: Little to no accurate representation of electron orbitals; energy levels are missing or entirely incorrect, and electron visualization does not reflect quantum mechanics.

prompts.subject: math
prompts.prompt_text: Generate a video visually showing fraction addition 1/2 + 1/4 using area models. Start with two identical rectangular bars. Shade 1/2 of the first bar and 1/4 of the second bar. Then show the first bar being divided into fourths to create a common denominator, revealing that 1/2 equals 2/4. Combine the shaded regions to show the result is 3/4.

ground_truth.correct_answer: 1/2 + 1/4 = 3/4, demonstrated through area model visualization

prompts.rubric_criteria: 9-10: Fraction bars are proportionally accurate, common denominator conversion is clear, final answer 3/4 is correctly shown and labeled. 7-8: Fraction bars are mostly accurate, common denominator conversion is shown but may lack clarity, final answer is correct but labeling could be improved. 5-6: Fraction bars are present but may have minor proportional inaccuracies, common denominator conversion is attempted but not fully clear, final answer is shown but lacks clear labeling. 3-4: Bars and shaded regions appear but proportions are incorrect or the common denominator step is missing. 1-2: Fraction bars are missing or highly inaccurate, common denominator conversion is not attempted, final answer is incorrect or not shown.

prompts.subject: science
prompts.prompt_text: Generate a video demonstrating the water electrolysis experiment step-by-step. ground_truth.correct_answer: Step-by-step demonstration of water electrolysis: 2H2O -> 2H2 + O2
key_steps: Turn on power and observe bubbles

prompts.rubric_criteria: 9-10: All experimental steps shown in correct order, gas collection is accurate with correct 2:1 volume ratio, electrode labeling (cathode/anode) is correct. 7-8: Most steps are shown in correct order, gas collection is mostly accurate with minor errors in volume ratio, electrode labeling is mostly correct. 5-6: Some steps are shown but may be out of order, gas collection has noticeable errors in volume ratio, electrode labeling is inconsistent. 3-4: Electrolysis setup shown but steps are incomplete, gas ratio is incorrect, or electrode labels are missing. 1-2: Few or no steps are shown, significant errors in setup and gas collection, electrode labeling is absent.

prompts.rubric_criteria: 9-10: Each algebraic step is clearly shown with correct mathematical operations, verification step included, step-by-step progression is easy to follow. 7-8: Most algebraic steps are shown correctly, with minor errors in operations or clarity; verification step is present but may lack detail. 5-6: Some algebraic steps are shown, but there are noticeable errors or omissions in operations; verification step may be incomplete or unclear. 3-4: Equations appear but solution steps contain errors or skip critical steps. 1-2: Few or no algebraic steps are shown, with significant errors or omissions; verification step is missing or incorrect.

key_visual_elements: dark top to light bottom gradient
